name: Apple Charlotka (Russian Apple Cake)
desc: Sliced tart apples baked under a whipped egg and sour cream batter.

source.title: Apple Charlotka (Russian apple cake)
source.evidence: Saved Instagram reel; caption and on-screen text captured in the owner's saved-recipes export

ingredients.raw: 8 large tart apples (such as Granny Smith), cored and thinly sliced
1 tbsp unsalted butter, softened, for the dish
10g vanilla sugar (or seeds of 1 vanilla bean)

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Butter a 9x13 in baking dish.
Core the apples and slice them thin, about 1/4 in (she uses a Tescoma Handy slicer). Toss with the lime juice.
Spread the apples evenly in the dish.
Beat the eggs on high about 1 min until foamy. With the mixer running, add the sugar, vanilla sugar and salt, then beat 8-10 min until pale and thick enough to fall in a ribbon.
Beat in the sour cream on low until just combined.
Sift the flour over the batter in 3 additions, folding gently after each until no streaks remain.
Pour the batter evenly over the apples.
Bake about 1 hr, until deep golden and a toothpick in the center comes out clean.
Rest in the dish at least 30 min so it sets before cutting.
tips: The caption says 10g of salt, about 1 3/4 tsp of fine salt, which is far more than most apple cakes use. If you would rather play it safe, use a pinch.
There is no baking powder; the long egg whipping is the only lift, so do not cut it short. Natasha's Kitchen's sharlotka whips 8-10 min and bakes 50-55 min at 350°F in a 9 in springform.
The dish size is an estimate; the reel shows a large buttered baking dish.

references.title: Easy Apple Cake (Sharlotka)
